video_title: Knicks Parade In NYC! + Is Parity BAD For NBA?

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on the Knicks' long-awaited championship and team personality
quotes.excerpt: This has been a long time coming, so the city absolutely deserves it. I'm excited for them.
quotes.quote: This is a long time coming, so the city absolutely deserves it. I'm excited for them. I think they'll put on a real show. The city will show out, the players will show out. You got some great personalities. Even since they won, we've seen these guys come out of their shells and show the other side of themselves and let their hair down. Mikal Bridges has been incredible on social media, Josh Hart remains a character in himself, same goes with Jalen Brunson. So I think it'll be a really good time.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams defends the current state of NBA league parity
quotes.excerpt: We champion so many different young stars, but the minute all of them start getting a piece
quotes.quote: Vince Goodwill believes parity is bad for the league and NBA championships are starting to feel like participation trophies. Do we agree? Do we disagree? I think that was one of the most outrageous things that you can hear. For me, it showed the strength in where we are in the league. We champion so many different young stars, but the minute all of them start getting a piece of the pie and start challenging each other for championships, now that's considered a bad thing.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins defends legacy of players without NBA championships
quotes.excerpt: When we start talking about the guys that didn't win championships and you're trying to say
quotes.quote: I disagree with the whole statement. It was a pretty crazy statement in the first place. At the end of the day, somebody has to win. But the weird part to me was talking about the validation part. Like, if you win a championship, the only way you can validate is if you win another one. So that's in a category of his own. But when we start talking about the guys that didn't win championships and you're trying to say they're not validated, so I think about guys like Charles Barkley, I think about the Allen Iversons, the Reggie Millers, the Tracy McGrady's, the Carmelo Anthony's, the list goes on, the Chris Paul's, and you sit here and you make a statement like that.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons emphasizes the difficulty of winning an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: When people speak on this sport, they have a tendency to water it down
quotes.quote: I think he doesn't understand how hard it is to win a game, let alone a series, let alone a championship in the NBA. And that's my issue with it as well. When people speak on this sport, they have a tendency to water it down and make it seem like it's just such a simple game, when there's so much work, blood, sweat, and tears that go into this game, especially at the highest level, the elite level of basketball.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on the betrayal felt by coaches after being fired
quotes.excerpt: I'd be sick, I'd be salty, and especially because him, he had a great five-year stint there.
quotes.quote: I'd be sick, I'd be salty, and especially because him, he had a great five-year stint there. He had a winning record. Obviously, he's a historic, great coach, and I think he just got away from the time. The league changed so much and Thibs, as good of a coach he is, he didn't want to roll with that. He said he wanted to play five, six guys. He didn't want to use his bench. He didn't want to use analytics. But he did have some great years there, and he made some playoff runs there, and he had a winning record as a head coach there, and then they replaced him with a guy that they won a championship the following year. That's got to sting a bit.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on why the Thunder wouldn't beat the Spurs if they swapped stars
quotes.excerpt: I don't want this to be a slight to Jalen Brunson because everything he does is phenomenal.
quotes.quote: I don't want this to be a slight to Jalen Brunson because everything he does is phenomenal, and he has put the Knicks back on the map and just willed them to a championship. No doubt. But to say this is just crazy. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is a stud. He's the back-to-back MVP, first team All-NBA player. He's the best player in the world, arguably. And Jalen Brunson is whatever, four, five, six, whatever you want to put him. I am just saying this is just another hot take that I feel like is clickbaity, and I don't even want to get into it because it's going to either be like I'm dissing Jalen Brunson by saying no, or dissing Shai Gilgeous-Alexander by saying yes. But no, it's just not true.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on the toxicity of comparing players and protecting legends
quotes.excerpt: We got to restore order in how we discuss our game, man.
quotes.quote: We had Patrick Beverley on yesterday, and for a minute we had a discussion about the James Harden take that he had. Now he's saying Jalen Brunson is better than Allen Iverson. I played with AI, and I just don't love this take. At some point, we got to start protecting our legends and their legacies. We can't just every time something happens, put their legacies on the chopping block to big up somebody else. It's okay to celebrate Jalen Brunson. It's okay to give him his flowers and his props without bringing anybody else or comparing anybody else. AI never had the teams that he had, and he still made it to the NBA Finals. It's no reason for this to even be a comparison and get people's blood pressure up about an argument that's a mute point.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on the celebrity culture surrounding the Knicks and Spike Lee
quotes.excerpt: I see Spike Lee on the court, and it's tight around the garden in terms of security.
quotes.quote: I don't get to New York very often, so it's funny because if you go to LA, you see all the celebrities, you kind of get used to that. The New York side with Spike Lee being at the top of that list, I was admitting to people that you're talking about like celebs that are right up like my generation's alleyway, like Spike, like come on. And getting to wrap and chopping it up with Ben Stiller in the back, stuff like that. So I see Spike Lee on the court, and it's tight around the garden in terms of security. Say hello to him real quick, said, 'Hey, just want to say hello, appreciate everything you've done,' and then introduced myself. And it doesn't matter how long you do this, if you meet somebody like that and they actually claim to know who you are and your work, he says, 'Oh, you're a great writer.' And it's funny because yes, it made my day.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on the Spurs' collapse and the Knicks' resilience
quotes.excerpt: It showed us the youth and the inexperience on the Spurs side, and then it showed the specialness.
quotes.quote: Man, DeMarcus, it was tough. My guy, Kawhi out of LA, Law Murray had a tweet yesterday that I thought captured it beautifully and kind of went viral. He said something like, 'It was the night that when Game 6 would have been.' And so out of nowhere, Law puts a tweet out that says, 'Right about now is when the Spurs would have given up a double-digit lead and lost Game 6.' It was just, it was just like, you know, wash, rinse, and repeat. And it did two things to me, like it showed us the youth and the inexperience on the Spurs side, and then it showed the specialness of this Knicks group and how they really were one of those teams that like, you know, if it's a boxing match, it could be 9th, 10th round, you've been getting beat up the whole time, and it's one of those fighters that you just can't sleep on because he's not going to go down and he's going to have something left. That's how the Knicks were.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on the Spurs' roster construction and De'Aaron Fox's contract
quotes.excerpt: It's one of the trickier situations that I've seen, and the reason is like I wrote about.
quotes.quote: It's one of the trickier situations that I've seen, and the reason is like I wrote about, like on the one hand you could look at it with glasses half full and say, 'All right, the Spurs, they've been through something like this before.' You had, you know, Mantas Janopoli, who was a starting caliber guard, and they convinced Manta to come off the bench and the rest is history. But the financial stuff was very different. You didn't, you weren't looking at a player like De'Aaron, who's on track to make $60 million and a guy like Dillon Harper who's on a rookie contract with this massive divide between these two talents. It's just not as simple as convincing De'Aaron to go to a reserve role, because first of all, I don't think he's ready for that yet. This is not somebody who's 33, 34 years old who's ready to shift into their post-prime years. He's in his prime.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on whether Victor Wembanyama is the NBA's new villain
quotes.excerpt: It feels like it, like fair or not, and a lot of it's fair, because you're talking about.
quotes.quote: It feels like it, like fair or not, and a lot of it's fair, because you're talking about a, you know, he got a highlight reel, he has no problem finding a highlight reel with, and a low-light reel with, you know, shoving Jalen's face all the way down to the hardwood and the elbow on Naz Reid in the previous rounds. And the one thing I have been saying to people in defense of Wemby, it's a little bit like with Shaq, like if you, one of these networks should have like a Wemby cam where if you want to, like the camera just stays on Wemby all the time so that we can at least see all the times that he's getting hit below the belt and hitting the head. Like he gets beat up the whole game, and then when he reacts, he's obviously not afraid to react strongly. And when it comes to the villain, you know, label, that's when I think a couple of things are in play. Like you're the guy who went against the beloved Knicks. Even if you're not a Knicks fan, this was a really popular, kind of America's team type of Knicks group, and so now you're the the guy going against him.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on Mike Brown's impact on the Knicks' team culture
quotes.excerpt: When the Knicks decided to hire Mike Brown, a major part of their reasoning was because he had.
quotes.quote: I admittedly like Thibs a lot, respect the heck out of him, incredible career. And when this topic comes up, like I'm not alone. People are kind of uncomfortable because it's hard to praise Mike without having it be in the context of criticizing Thibs. And considering what he poured into that program, like that's tough. But it's also, this is the story, this is what happened. And reality is that when the Knicks decided to hire Mike Brown, a major part of their reasoning was because he had the type of personality and collaborative nature that they felt like they were lacking. As close as Thibs was with that whole group, he had times, you know, in his whole career, he's kind of been known to be one of those like, 'batten down the hatches, my way or the highway' type coaches. And the front office, even Jim Dolan, they wanted to have their voices be heard. The players, you know, at times wanted to have their voices be heard. And Mike represented all of that.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on Jalen Brunson's case for greatest Knick of all time
quotes.excerpt: The argument for Jalen is that this Knicks team, the help around him outside of Cat, does not compare.
quotes.quote: I feel like it's one of the the rare ones where I feel like I'm I'm not equipped to like I'm young enough, which is not something I say much these days, to to like I don't know. Can I weigh in on on, you know, on Clyde, can I weigh in on on those guys? I mean, you got two championships with loaded teams. The argument for Jalen is that this Knicks team, the help around him outside of Cat, does not compare to what those teams in the old days had for the Knicks. And so that augments Jalen's case. I mean, he's in the conversation. You know, when his own father is saying that that Patrick is the guy, maybe he's just trying to to to give love to his buddy. But I mean, Patrick, his case is tricky because longevity-wise, impact-wise, you know, he beat everybody, but he didn't win the chip, which as an aside, it was so cool to see Patrick kind of lean into that experience the other night and actually hold the trophy and and, you know, live vicariously through these guys.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on the possibility of the Wizards trading Trae Young
quotes.excerpt: It feels like a little bit of leverage play for me, that, you know, Trae wants to make sure.
quotes.quote: It feels like a little bit of leverage play for me, that, you know, Trae wants to make sure the Wizards, you know, take care of him. I mean, when when he went that direction, it felt like there was already a handshake deal in place. You know, and and especially when it seemed like he was healthy enough to play, and then he wasn't playing, it it kind of added fuel to that fire where, you know, you guys know this stuff happens all the time. Like, all right, you know, we need to drop some games this year, get the number one pick, uh, but here's what we got for you on the back end. So I'm a little bit surprised that there's as much noise around Trae as there is. It could be the the ripple effect of, like if you got Anthony Davis there who's not sure that he wants to be there and Trae, you know, maybe doesn't see the the chance to contend like he did when the AD deal first went down and he thought he'd be rocking with the big fella.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick's predictions for the NBA draft night trades
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to go with Peterson and say they do the Bailey thing and just, you know, push right through it.
quotes.quote: Not our resident draft expert, but tuned in enough that I can take a guess. I mean, I got Bonza first. I honestly, you know, with the Jazz, uh, I'm going to go with Peterson and say they do the Bailey thing and just, you know, push right through it. And then, you know, Memphis has been tied to Boozer for a long time. So, I think the the one thing as a subplot that I did kind of love and I don't know if I'm reading the room the right way, but when it comes to the Jazz, you had a a funny couple days of news, guys, where it was like, 'All right, Peterson doesn't want to work out, that makes the Jazz kind of look bad.' Then, I wrote the Walker Kessler thing, he's frustrated. Then, the the story you mentioned, Chandler, what I kind of loved about it in terms of just the chessboard and in the way the media comes into play here, is like the Jazz immediately getting it out there that they're seriously considering Cam Boozer to me felt very much like, 'Hey Walker, you know, look how easy it would be to to go get a big, you know, who could take your job and be a whole lot cheaper.'

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on the likelihood of LeBron James and Austin Reaves returning to the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I'll put it, I mean, I probably a six, if if we're talking about both.
quotes.quote: I'll put it, I mean, I probably a six, if if we're talking about both. I know, I mean, that the Austin one, I think it's done. Man, it's just like, it's hard, like it's and even I know it's a different level of player, but like they got Rui Hachimura is up too, right? And what keeps striking me about the Lakers situation is like, man, you got every player who's up, and I'm all for guys getting paid, but here's, this is probably not fair, but quick backdrop. You guys know like we just celebrated the Knicks championship. Jalen Brunson, you know, took a $113 million sacrifice, and and it certainly helped their team. And again, as an aside, Jim Dolan, maybe be quiet about not wanting to pay in the second apron because your guy gave up $100 million. But that's a different story. You had sacrifice from a player. Now, the Lakers, it it's challenging because they have got to get better. And if they just resign LeBron, resign Austin, resign Rui, that's not getting better, that's maintaining, right? Well, all of their guys are signaling like, 'I will stay if you don't disrespect me with the number.' Like that's basically kind of what the the shared messaging is, and that makes me think that in terms of the way, you know, DeMarcus, that you frame the question, if you're talking about both guys, I think if Austin gets paid in the kind of way that keeps him in town, then there's not enough money for LeBron to feel respected.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Amick on the Lakers' financial constraints and LeBron James' future
quotes.excerpt: I think if Austin gets paid in the kind of way that keeps him in town, then there's not enough money for LeBron.
quotes.quote: I think if Austin gets paid in the kind of way that keeps him in town, then there's not enough money for LeBron to feel respected, and then I could see him going up the coast and maybe doing the Warriors thing. Um, you know, so I I feel like there's just not enough money to make all those guys happy with the Lakers. Got you.
